title: Efficient Training-Free Multi-Token Prediction via Embedding-Space Probing
claim: Standard one-token decoding extends to parallel multi-token prediction by appending probe tokens and verifying drafts in a single tree-masked pass.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right progression, attention-mask matrices beneath each panel
description: Three side-by-side panels show an LLM as a wide white box, with input tokens below it and output tokens above it, joined by dashed arrows. Left: standard next-token prediction. Blue tokens x1…xt go in and a single x_{t+1} comes out. Middle: extra purple mask tokens m1 and m2 are appended to the prompt, so the LLM also outputs orange predicted tokens x̂_{t+2} and x̂_{t+3}. Right: the verification and generation stage. It has a longer input row of blue, orange and purple tokens, including x_s, x̂_{s+1}, x̂_{s+2} and several m tokens. Green checks and red X marks show accepted and rejected drafts, and red question marks mark the verification arrows. Under each panel, a staircase-shaped block matrix shows the attention mask. The left and middle masks are causal. The right mask is a sparse tree mask. The colors blue, orange and purple mark real, drafted and mask tokens.
caption: (Left) Standard next-token prediction setup for autoregressive models, (middle) multi-token prediction during prefill-stage by probing mask tokens which are appended to prompt tokens, (right) multi-token prediction with parallel verification and generation. Mask tokens are associated with last generated token (xs) and future tokens (ˆxs+1, ˆxs+2) through custom tree attention mask.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) possess latent multi-token prediction (MTP) abilities despite being trained only for next-token generation. We introduce ESP (Embedding-Space Probing), a simple and training-free MTP method that probes an LLM using on-the-fly mask tokens drawn from its embedding space, enabling parallel future-token prediction without modifying weights or relying on draft models. ESP constructs a speculative token tree by sampling Top-K candidates from mask-token logits and applies a lightweight pruning rule to retain high-probability continuations. During generation, predictions are verified in parallel, yielding lossless decoding while significantly reducing model calls and increasing token throughput. ESP consistently outperforms existing training-free baselines, improving acceptance length by 7-11% over LADE on LLaMA3 and 7-8% on Qwen3, and increasing throughput by up to 15-19% over the strongest baseline. Finally, we provide theoretical insight and empirical evidence showing that decoder layers naturally align mask-token representations with next-token states, enabling accurate multi-step prediction without retraining or auxiliary models.
